an6.43:1.1: On one occasion the Blessed One was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
an6.43:1.2: Then early in the morning the Blessed One adjusted his under robe and—carrying his bowl & robes—went into Sāvatthī for alms.
an6.43:1.3: After his meal, on returning from his alms round, he addressed Ven. Ānanda,
an6.43:1.4: “Come, Ānanda, let’s go to the Eastern Monastery, the palace of Migāra’s mother, for the day’s abiding.”
an6.43:1.5: “As you say, lord,” Ven. Ānanda responded to the Blessed One.
an6.43:2.1: Then the Blessed One together with Ven. Ānanda went to the Eastern Monastery, the palace of Migāra’s mother.
an6.43:2.2: On emerging from his seclusion in the late afternoon, he addressed Ven. Ānanda,
an6.43:2.3: “Come, Ānanda, let’s go to the Eastern Gatehouse to bathe our limbs.”
an6.43:2.4: “As you say, lord,” Ven. Ānanda responded to the Blessed One.
an6.43:2.5: Then the Blessed One together with Ven. Ānanda went to the Eastern Gatehouse to bathe his limbs.
an6.43:2.6: Having bathed his limbs near the Eastern Gatehouse and gotten out of the water, he stood wearing only his lower robe, letting his limbs dry.
an6.43:3.1: Then King Pasenadi Kosala’s nāga elephant named Seta came out of the Eastern Gatehouse accompanied by a great noise of instruments & drums.
an6.43:3.3: “How beautiful is the king’s nāga! How lovely the king’s nāga! How inspiring the king’s nāga! How blessed with a body the king’s nāga!”
an6.43:3.4: When this was said, Ven. Udāyin said to the Blessed One,
an6.43:3.5: “Lord, is it only on seeing an elephant blessed with a large, massive body that people say,
an6.43:3.6: ‘A nāga! What a nāga!’? Or is there anything else blessed with a large, massive body that people, on seeing it, say, ‘A nāga! What a nāga!’?”
an6.43:3.7: “Udāyin, it’s on seeing an elephant blessed with a large, massive body that that people say,
an6.43:3.9: It’s on seeing a horse blessed with a large, massive body,
an6.43:3.10: a bull blessed with a large, massive body,
an6.43:3.11: a serpent blessed with a large, massive body,
an6.43:3.12: a tree blessed with a large, massive body,
an6.43:3.13: a human being blessed with a large, massive body that people say,
an6.43:3.15: “But, Udāyin, whoever in this world with its devas, Māras, & Brahmās, in this generation with its contemplatives & brahmans, its royalty & commonfolk—does no misdeed in body, speech, or mind: That’s whom I call a nāga.”
an6.43:4.2: How that was well-said by the Blessed One:
an6.43:4.3: ‘But, Udāyin, whoever in this world with its devas, Māras, & Brahmās, in this generation with its contemplatives & brahmans, its royalty & commonfolk, does no misdeed in body, speech, or mind:
an6.43:4.4: That’s whom I call a nāga.’ And with these verses, lord, I will rejoice in what was well-said by the Blessed One:
an6.43:5.4: delighting in the stilling of the mind:
an6.43:6.1: He, having gone beyond all dhammas,
an6.43:6.2: to whom human beings pay homage,
an6.43:6.3: the devas pay homage as well—
an6.43:6.4: so I have heard from the Worthy One
an6.43:7.2: gone from the forest to the clearing,3
an6.43:7.3: delighting in the renunciation of sensuality,
an6.43:7.4: released like gold from its ore.
an6.43:8.1: He, the nāga outshining all others,
an6.43:9.1: I will praise the nāga to you—
an6.43:10.2: are the nāga’s two other feet.
an6.43:10.3: Conviction is the great nāga’s trunk, his hand;
an6.43:11.1: Mindfulness his neck; his head, discernment,
an6.43:11.3: Dhamma the balanced heat of his digestion;
an6.43:12.1: He, in jhāna, delighting in assurance,
an6.43:12.3: the nāga, when going, is concentrated,
an6.43:12.4: when standing, the nāga is concentrated,
an6.43:13.1: when reclining, the nāga is concentrated,
an6.43:13.2: when sitting, the nāga is concentrated.
an6.43:16.3: but not smeared by the water
an6.43:17.1: even so the awakened one, well-born in the world,
an6.43:17.3: but is not smeared by the world,
an6.43:17.4: like the lotus, by the water.
